Consult Summary:
50-year-old man with type 2 diabetes and hypertension presents via telephone with 4–5 days of “flu-like” illness: predominantly dry cough, runny nose, sore throat, low-grade fevers/rigors, mild shortness of breath, and generalized myalgias/stiffness; clinician impression is viral upper respiratory infection with delayed prescription for amoxicillin if no improvement in 24–48 h.

History:
• Onset: Symptoms began Saturday (≈4–5 days ago).  
• Course: Persistent; no significant improvement yet.  
• Primary symptoms:  
  – Cough predominantly dry; mild sputum in mornings.  
  – Runny nose/congestion with audible sniffles.  
  – Sore throat (exacerbated by shouting at football).  
  – Subjective fevers/temperature fluctuations with night sweats.  
  – Mild shortness of breath without chest pain.  
  – Generalized joint/muscle stiffness.  
• Associated/other symptoms:  
  – One episode of self-limited diarrhea on first day.  
  – No nausea, vomiting, or abdominal pain currently.  
  – No ear pain of significance; slight dullness.  
• ROS pertinent negatives: No chest pain, no persistent GI symptoms other than stated, appetite preserved.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: Rest and fluids help; no clear triggers identified.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus – on metformin; no complications discussed.  
• Hypertension – on lisinopril.  
• Overweight/obesity (patient describes “spare tyre”).  

Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Aspirin as needed – dose/route/frequency not documented.  

Allergies:
• No known drug allergies (NKDA).

Social History:
• Lives with wife; children live independently.  
• Employment: Factory worker manufacturing steel parts.  
• Alcohol: ≈9 pints beer/week (4 on Saturday, remainder Sunday).  
• Tobacco: Occasional cigarettes; transitioning to vaping to reduce use.  
• No illicit drug use mentioned.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Telephone consult only; no vitals provided.  
• Audible nasal congestion noted by clinician.  
• No other objective findings documented.

Investigations:
• None performed/available.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Viral upper respiratory tract infection / possible early influenza
  – Supportive care: rest, adequate hydration, regular paracetamol for fever/aches.  
  – Safety-net advice: If worsening shortness of breath, persistent fever, or new symptoms, seek medical review.  

Issue 2: Possible secondary bacterial chest infection (not currently evident)
  – Delayed antibiotic prescription: Amoxicillin 1 tablet three times daily; start if no improvement within 24–48 h or clinical deterioration.  

Issue 3: Chronic conditions (T2DM, HTN, overweight)
  – Continue current medications (metformin, lisinopril).  
  – Encourage continued efforts to reduce smoking/vaping transition.  
  – Limit alcohol intake as previously advised.  
  – Routine follow-up with primary care for diabetes and blood pressure monitoring (not specifically scheduled today).

General Plan items:
• Follow-up: Return for review next week if not improved or sooner if symptoms escalate.  
• Educational reinforcement: Maintain good fluid intake, monitor temperature if possible, and rest.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: Objective vitals, physical examination, medication doses/frequencies, recent blood glucose/BP readings, vaccination status (e.g., influenza).  
● Internal conflicts: Patient initially says breathing “fine,” later states “not good” → conflict noted; clinician treated as mild SOB.  
● Transcript quality: Clear overall; some conversational digressions but clinically understandable; no audio gaps affecting data capture.
